messages:
Maya: FYI customer hit a 422 and then all-zero scores from the ranking endpoint when they switched from our SDK to a raw curl call.
Maya: Pasting the minimal payload they say reproduces it (they removed auth + ids):
```json
{
  "query": "how to reset password",
  "documents": [
    {
      "id": "doc-1",
      "title": "Reset guide",
      "query": "reset instructions",
      "text": "Step 1: click..."
    }
  ],
  "candidates": [
    {
      "id": "cand-1",
      "text": "You can reset via settings..."
    }
  ]
}
```
Maya: They said it worked earlier but after a refactor of their payload builder it started returning 422s and sometimes scores of 0.0 for every candidate.
Jordan: Can you get their full request-id from the logs (x-request-id) and the exact curl they ran? 422 + zeros smells like our server couldn't locate the root query and fell back to an empty string.
Ashley: Customer gave this curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ranking -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @payload.json
```
Ashley: payload.json was the JSON Maya pasted.
Jordan: Ah — nested key collision. We treat top-level "query" as the query text. But if there is also a "query" inside a document object our parser currently lets the nested one shadow/override during internal flattening in specific codepaths (esp. batch path used by raw HTTP). That leads to inconsistent behavior and sometimes an empty root query when the flatten step fails -> zero scores or 422 if validations hit.
Maya: Is this a known bug or is the customer doing something unsupported?
Jordan: It's a bug on our side. The SDK normalizer was masking it by always constructing a canonical top-level query; raw payloads that accidentally include a conflicting nested field can trip the runtime. Workarounds: 1) Move the user's search text to the top-level `query` (already done here but shadowing is coming from nested `documents[*].query`) or 2) rename nested field to `excerpt` / `snippet` or 3) wrap passages as `passages: [{text:...}]` and avoid `query` inside docs.
Ashley: Sent steps to customer: remove `query` from inside each document, re-run. They reported immediate success after renaming to `snippet`.
SupportBot: Linked internal incident INS-4321 and created a follow-up task: https://redwood.internal/ins/INS-4321 (private). @eng-runtime please triage.
Jordan: From an engineering perspective: we'll harden the request schema to reject nested `query` keys (422 with clear message) and add a normalization pass that prefers the explicit top-level `query` if present. I'll open PR to fail-fast and include a migration note for SDKs. Expected timeline: patch this week, deploy next canary.
Maya: Customer is happy with the workaround and asked for a short note to include in their changelog. I told them we'll follow up when the server enforces the check.
Jordan: Quick debug log snippet from the failing instance for record:
```
[2026-03-16T14:22:01Z] request-id=abc123 parsing payload: found key\u003dquery at path documents.0.query -> shadow candidate for root.query
[2026-03-16T14:22:01Z] request-id=abc123 validation: root.query empty -> returning 200 with zero scores
```
Jordan: Note the weird branch where we returned 200 with zero scores instead of 422 — that's also on the list to fix (should be an error when root query is empty and no fallback).
Ashley: I'll mark the support ticket as "patched-by-customer workaround" and leave the internal ticket open until eng confirms the server fix.
Maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
